reviewQuestion: Can an operator distinguish whole-meeting deletion from audio-only release, understand the exact terminal scope, cancel safely, and resume one interrupted deletion without exposing the affected meeting in current Find, Meetings, or Promises results?

evidenceBasis.market: Corpus retrieval is positioned as core value; documented comparables expose multiple retrieval entry points.
evidenceBasis.scopeBoundary: The first beta uses exact transcript-and-metadata search; conversational cross-meeting answers remain later scope.

reviewControl: The dark comparison bar changes only the default opening view; the light app header is the proposed persistent product navigation.

activeContentSlice.surveyBasis: Sales or discovery calls were selected by 3 of 3 respondents.

trustSetupSlice.placement: Settings is a utility surface outside the accepted Find, Meetings, and Promises navigation.
contracts: Start requires both permissions, an explicit retention period, and a valid profile.
A new retention choice has no default.
Profile reset preserves meetings, notes, transcripts, retained meeting audio, and retention choice.
A returning-profile fixture is independent from new enrollment and cannot complete it.
The second sitting requires a measured gap of at least one hour; the fixture never claims real time elapsed.
Comparison speech must be public-domain, appropriately licensed, or deliberately recorded by a consenting person.
No measured policy is selected or recommended by default.
Dedicated source audio and working files are represented as deleted after safe private derivation.
Start remains blocked until the selected row and provenance are represented as owner-only persisted.
Discard preserves meetings, meeting audio, notes, transcripts, retention choice, and any previously valid profile.
Restoring a withheld turn creates a successor canonical transcript view rather than rewriting the captured transcript.
The prior note remains readable as stale history but is excluded from current results.
No partial replacement note becomes current after the request-only interruption.
Each document reload returns to the affected meeting with one safe action until note regeneration reaches a terminal state.
The header blocks a new meeting while recovery needs attention, then returns to Start after version 2 becomes current.
The recovery reader rejects unknown receipt fields before restoring synthetic state.
The synthetic receipt stores no transcript, note, meeting title, or private content.

wholeMeetingDeletionSlice.placement: Meeting detail only; distinct from the reviewed immediate audio-only release control.
contracts: The scope review names every terminal consequence and does not use vague data language.
A second, explicit acknowledgement is required before either the terminal action or reviewer interruption control is enabled.
Cancellation leaves the synthetic meeting unchanged and is labelled as keeping the meeting.
The reviewer interruption persists only a content-free request receipt before document reload; it does not complete deletion or publish a partial current meeting.
Reset task, default-opening controls, product navigation, Settings, and Start retain a pending operation and return to its recovery surface.

Unknown receipt fields, invalid values, mixed recovery receipts, and unreadable session envelopes fail closed by retaining raw browser-storage evidence, withholding possibly affected meetings, and routing to blocked recovery.
Blocked recovery offers only a staged reviewer-only full fixture repair; it is explicitly not product behavior and cannot silently clear valid operations.
While request-only recovery is pending, the affected meeting, transcript-derived search hits, note claims, and recorded promises are unavailable in Find, Meetings, and Promises.
A second reload reconstructs the same one-action recovery surface; resume is idempotent and clears the receipt only after terminal completion.
Retention, released-audio, correction, voice-profile, permission, and unrelated-meeting state survive interrupted deletion and terminal completion.
Terminal completion validates and reads back a session-state tombstone before clearing the request; later document reloads cannot resurrect the meeting.
Terminal deletion does not offer undo or imply recovery of the removed meeting content.
Deletion and blocked-recovery headings receive focus and are scrolled into the internal pane; the outer 960x900 page remains fixed.
